attributes.title: Level 4

subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you change the number of times the program loops through setting and placing the Gold sprite?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which block changes how many times code blocks are run in a project?


Solution: 

The parameter in the [repeat] loop should be changed from “2” to “4”.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there are only 2 Gold sprites for the Player sprite to collect on the screen. 


Fix the bugs in the code so that the Player sprite has 4 Gold sprites to collect.

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the correct number of sprites appear on the screen and a screen effect shares a hint about each sprite’s location.

validationItems.text: Parameter in the [repeat] loop is changed from “2” to “4”.
validationItems.failureText: Check the parameter in the [repeat] loop.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓ Which sprite array should the [for element] loop reveal a hint for?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓Which sprite kind should be selected in the (array of sprites of kind) block?


Solution: 

The sprite kind selected in the (array of sprites of kind) block should be changed from “Player” to “Gold”.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, only 1 hint is revealed about the Gold sprites’ locations.


Fix the bugs in the code so that the project reveals hints for all 4 of the Gold sprites that are hidden on the tilemap.

namespace SpriteKind {
    export const Gold = SpriteKind.create()
}
sprites.onOverlap(SpriteKind.Player, SpriteKind.Gold, function (sprite, otherSprite) {
    if (controller.A.isPressed()) {
        otherSprite.setFlag(SpriteFlag.Invisible, false)
        otherSprite.setFlag(SpriteFlag.Ghost, true)
        foundGold.push(otherSprite)
    }
    if (foundGold.length == sprites.allOfKind(SpriteKind.Gold).length) {
        pause(1000)
        game.gameOver(true)
    }
})

        . . b b b . . . 
        . b 5 5 5 b . . 
        b 5 d 3 d 5 b . 
        b 5 3 5 1 5 b . 
        c 5 3 5 1 d c . 
        c 5 d 1 d d c . 
        . f d d d f . . 
        . . f f f . . . 
        `, SpriteKind.Gold)
    hiddenGold.setFlag(SpriteFlag.Invisible, true)
    tiles.placeOnRandomTile(hiddenGold, sprites.castle.tilePath5)
}
let goldMiner = sprites.create(img`

    `, SpriteKind.Player)
controller.moveSprite(goldMiner)
foundGold = []
info.startCountdown(20)
game.onUpdateInterval(5000, function () {
    for (let value of sprites.allOfKind(SpriteKind.Player)) {
        hiddenGold.startEffect(effects.halo, 100)
    }
})
forever(function () {
    goldMiner.say("" + foundGold.length + "/" + sprites.allOfKind(SpriteKind.Gold).length)
})

Ask the ninja: 

❓Which variable should be used in the [sprite start effect] block, so that each Gold sprite shares a hint on the screen?


Solution: 

A (value) bubble from the [for element] loop is dragged into the variable bubble of the [sprite start effect] block.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, the hints about the Gold sprites’ locations still don’t appear in the right position on the tilemap!


Fix the bugs in the code so that each Gold sprite on the tilemap gives a hint about its location through the halo effect.

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the correct number of sprites appear on the screen and a screen effect shares a hint about each sprite’s location.

validationItems.text: (value) bubble dragged into [sprite start effect] block in the [for element] loop.
validationItems.failureText: Check the variable selected in the [sprite start effect] block.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 4 of Orange Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about repeat and for loops. A loop is a chunk of code that repeats until a specific condition is met. You’ll use what you already know about variables and arrays to create loops that respond to specific conditions. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level #4:

badges.title: Deja Vu
badges.description: Use different types of loops to repeat code in a project.

badges.title: Once More, With Feeling
badges.description: Use a repeat loop to repeat code a given number of times.

badges.title: Yearbook
badges.description: Create and use an array of sprites.

badges.title: Roll Call
badges.description: Use a for element of loop to make something happen to each item in an array.

badges.title: Freeze Tag
badges.description: Use a pause in a project.

badges.title: Button Down
badges.description: Check if a button is being pressed before making something happen in a project.
